title: Attention Is All You Need for Multimodal Reasoning: A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. In this work, we present an exhaustive study on how self-attention mechanisms scale to multimodal vision-language representations, offering state-of-the-art inference efficiency and benchmark robustness.

title: LoRA-XS: Low-Rank Adaptation with Extremely Small Parameter Footprint
abstract: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has become the gold standard for adapting large foundation models to downstream domain tasks. We propose LoRA-XS, a structural matrix factorization technique reducing trainable rank dimensions by 70% while matching dense fine-tuning perplexity across GLUE and MMLU benchmarks.

title: Diffusion-Based Generative Agents for Interactive Multi-Agent Game Environments
abstract: Generative agents simulate believable human behavior by populating interactive virtual environments. In this paper, we replace traditional autoregressive planning with continuous diffusion trajectories, enabling real-time multi-agent negotiation, spatial memory retrieval, and emergent social coordination.

title: Vision-Language State Space Models for Long-Horizon Video Understanding
abstract: Transformer architectures struggle with quadratic complexity when scaling to hour-long video contexts. We introduce Mamba-Vision, a selective state-space model that processes video tokens in linear time while maintaining cross-modal semantic retrieval comparable to ViT-H/14 models.

title: Direct Preference Optimization via Offline Contrastive Margin Alignments
abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) often introduces training instability through policy reward models. Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) implicitly optimizes the policy using closed-form classification loss. We extend DPO to non-stationary preference distributions with margin decay bounds.
